name: Rémi Bardenet
body:
Thanks Pierre for an interesting post on a difficult and polarizing question. On my end, if I accept the premise of forgetting about "ecological, economic, social, political, moral, sovereignty, privacy" concerns, I agree with you: if we think hard on what we want to preserve as we incorporate LLMs and coding agents, I can see a possible future where we perform better research. And I mean better both in terms of results and process, at least in CS/maths. But I have major issues with the premise. 

In many scenarios, the price that society will pay for its systematic adoption of AI assistance is frightening. By making LLMs and coding agents daily companions for my research, and thus implicitly backing up their wide adoption by the people around me, my individual research output may well increase, but I am concerned that my expected contribution to society may decrease, however we may reasonably measure it. On the other hand, it is a disguised arms race, and I am also worried that we (France, the EU) might be missing a strategic train if we take too much time to think.

This makes me think a lot on how we should regulate the development and the use of these tools, and what my own responsibility is in all this. I am also worried that I don't see the question being publicly discussed by our institutions.
